item.title: Alleged Mortgage Fraud Exposed: Lawsuits detail DSCR loan flips; Baltimore housing suffers
item.description: In 2022, a property in Baltimore purchased for $43,000 astonishingly changed hands for $310,000 just a year later. This sharp spike in valuation has led to accusations of inflated property prices by investors, resulting in numerous foreclosures. Federal lawsuits allege a scheme involving over 150 properties generating millions in loans, prompting lender scrutiny and investigations into the housing market, revealing Baltimore's deep-seated issues with housing insecurity. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: 170-year-old portrait sold for $882 in 2025 fetches $230,400 after man's identity is discovered
item.description: A photograph that fetched $882 at a New York auction last year has now been identified as a portrait of George Boyer Vashon, the first licensed African American lawyer in New York State. Experts recognized its historical significance, leading Sotheby's to auction it for an astonishing $230,400, far surpassing its initial estimate. This revelation underscores the profound impact of historical context on art valuation. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: ¿Por qué quisiera Meta que gane Flávio Bolsonaro en Brasil?
item.description: ¿Puede una plataforma digital alterar el equilibrio de una elección presidencial? En Brasil, la campaña de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva acusa a Meta, propietaria de Instagram, Facebook y WhatsApp, de perjudicar sus contenidos y dar mayor visibilidad a los vinculados a su rival, Flávio Bolsonaro. Mensajes internos publicados por 'Folha de S.Paulo' apuntan a que empleados de la compañía detectaron restricciones que afectaban a la campaña de Lula y recomendaciones algorítmicas favorables al candidato del Partido Liberal.
